clue.text: It may be blocked for dancers

definitions.text: It may be blocked for dancers

blocks.clueFragment: It may be blocked for dancers
blocks.note: surface reading: something, perhaps a stage exit or a road, that gets obstructed and holds up the dancers
setter's reading: a ballerina's pointe footwear has a stiffened box toe, called a block

explanation.surface: Something obstructs a troupe of dancers on their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocked' suggests an obstruction; in ballet a pointe shoe is 'blocked', built with a hard toe box so the dancer can stand on tiptoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointe footwear worn by ballerinas has a stiffened toe box, which is literally described as blocked.

clue.text: Stop when the standard is low

blocks.note: first meaning: to signal a vehicle such as a taxi to halt
second meaning: a standard is a flag, and here it hangs lowered

explanation.surface: Someone is told to halt whenever quality drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' looks like a level of quality, but it is a banner on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Waving at a passing car to make it halt is a phrasal verb, and a lowered banner is literally in that state.

clue.text: Lose the point and go for the runs

blocks.note: first meaning: in tennis or squash, sending the ball beyond the lines concedes the rally
second meaning: in cricket, a batsman who swings aggressively to score quickly

explanation.surface: Someone misses the argument and then dashes off to the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The runs' hints at a stomach upset, but runs are cricket's scoring units; to bat aggressively for them is the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Striking a ball beyond the court boundary forfeits a rally, while a cricketer attacking the bowling for quick scoring does the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: The chances of racing

blocks.note: surface reading: the prospects of the sport of racing surviving or succeeding
setter's reading: the bookmaker's prices quoted on each horse in a race

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up the future of horse racing as a sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookmakers express the likelihood of each runner winning as betting prices such as five to one.

clue.text: Place a posy, put out for the unveiling

indicators.note: something put out is disturbed or upset, so the letters before it are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters of these three words, taken together

explanation.surface: Flowers are laid out ready for a memorial's unveiling ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The unveiling sounds like a plaque ceremony; the answer's Greek root means uncovering, the name of the Book of Revelation.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek word behind it literally means an uncovering or revelation, the title of the Bible's final book.

clue.text: Sea dog in trouble in California

definitions.note: names a place found in that state rather than a synonym for it

indicators.note: letters in trouble are in a mess, so they are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, and also read as part of the indicator

explanation.surface: An old sailor has got into difficulties on the Californian coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' does double duty, joining the jumbled letters and starting the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a large port city on the Pacific coast of that state, near the Mexican border.

clue.text: Tax put on new car stock

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the word after it is rearranged
one item is added onto another, so the pieces are simply joined

blocks.note: the letters of this word rearranged
value added tax, the British sales tax

explanation.surface: A dealer adds sales tax to the price of fresh cars in the showroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like a dealer's inventory, but a stock is also a stiff wide neckcloth.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock was a wide band of cloth worn around the neck, much like a man's scarf-style necktie.

clue.text: Better the non-drinker leaves this

indicators.note: when someone leaves they are taken away, so their letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: It is wiser if the abstainer stays away from this drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the abstainer's TT from the middle of the first word and what is left is the drink itself, which a teetotaller would indeed leave alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotaller refuses alcoholic drinks such as ale or lager, so the whole clue describes the brew.

clue.text: Everyone bound to be properly organised

blocks.note: all means every person
bound with rope or string

explanation.surface: Everybody is obliged to keep things neat and orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: When arrangements are fully settled and nothing is left loose, the informal phrase says they are sorted.

clue.text: About time to go out -- OK?

indicators.note: one word going outside the other means it wraps around it

blocks.note: an age is a long period of time
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether it is finally time to head out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time' reads as a phrase of impatience, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying okay signals consent, just as a verb meaning to concur or accept does.

clue.text: Safe anchorages found on entering Nigerian port

indicators.note: a word entering another goes inside it

blocks.note: Lagos is Nigeria's largest city and main port
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sheltered moorings are discovered at a West African harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow stretches of water cut off from the sea by reefs or sandbars give boats sheltered places to moor.

clue.text: Stiff man enters vehicle

indicators.note: the man enters the vehicle, so his name sits inside it

blocks.note: a car is a road vehicle
a man's name

explanation.surface: A man with a stiff back climbs awkwardly into a car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff' looks like an adjective, but it is slang for a dead body.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiff is a slang noun for a corpse, and the answer is the formal word for a dead human body.

clue.text: Old woman tickled to death?

blocks.note: first meaning: a disparaging term for a crabby elderly woman
second meaning: a fish caught by tickling, stroking it by hand until it can be grabbed

explanation.surface: An elderly lady is hugely amused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tickled to death' means delighted, but tickling is a way of catching a river fish by hand, which ends in its death.
explanation.definitionFit: Old trout is an unkind British phrase for a grumpy elderly woman, and this freshwater fish is famously caught by hand-tickling.

clue.text: A smokescreen?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cover of smoke laid to hide troops, or a deception
setter's reading: a screen that sieves the smoke drawn through a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: A smokescreen is a deception, but read literally it is a sieve for smoke, which is what the end of some cigarettes does.
explanation.definitionFit: The mouth end of many cigarettes holds a fibrous plug that traps tar and particles before the smoker inhales.

clue.text: A relatively bitter struggle

blocks.note: surface reading: a fight that is fairly fierce, though not the worst
setter's reading: a fight among relatives, kin against kin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Relatively' seems to mean 'fairly', but it means 'between relatives'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running quarrel between kinsfolk, often bitter and bearing grudges across generations.

clue.text: Ineffective players seen going to train

blocks.note: first meaning: team members who contribute nothing and are carried by the rest
second meaning: people heading for a railway train to ride on it

explanation.surface: Weak members of the squad are spotted heading off to practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Train' suggests sports practice, but it is the railway kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Team members who are carried by others are called this, and so are travellers riding a train.

clue.text: What highly attractive investments may yield?

definitions.text: What highly attractive investments may yield?

blocks.clueFragment: What highly attractive investments may yield?
blocks.note: surface reading: the returns from appealing financial investments
setter's reading: good-looking, as a fine-looking face is attractive

explanation.walkthrough: The first word of the answer means good-looking as well as generous, so attractive investments give returns of both kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: Large and generous financial gains, described with an adjective that also means good-looking.

clue.text: Immersed, cooked and gently boiled

indicators.note: cooked figures are doctored, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recipe step: food dunked in water, cooked and gently boiled.
explanation.definitionFit: Heated just below a full bubbling boil, the gentle technique used for stews and sauces.

clue.text: Apt to be not on the level

blocks.note: first meaning: likely or disposed to do something
second meaning: sloping, not horizontal

explanation.surface: Someone is likely to be dishonest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on the level' suggests dishonesty, but here it means simply sloping.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed towards something is having a tendency, and a slope or tilted surface is at an angle.

clue.text: At home in France

blocks.note: surface reading: comfortable and settled in the French countryside
setter's reading: the phrase for being at home with one's kin, as a French speaker would say it

explanation.walkthrough: 'At home in France' reads as feeling settled there, but it asks for the French phrase meaning at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression means with the family, in an informal domestic setting, and English has borrowed it.

clue.text: Think of a number

blocks.note: first meaning: to reckon or conclude
second meaning: a numeral or digit

explanation.surface: The familiar opening of a party trick: pick any number in your head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think of a number' is a single familiar phrase, but split into two meanings joined by 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: As an informal verb it means to reckon or suppose, and as a noun it is a written numeral.

clue.text: Hiding place many yearn to find

definitions.text: Hiding place many yearn to find

blocks.clueFragment: Hiding place many yearn to find
blocks.note: surface reading: a secret spot that lots of people would love to discover
setter's reading: a hidden hoard of treasure or valuables, and the word sounds like money

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a hidden store, often of treasure, and it is pronounced like the money everyone wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret store of valuables, weapons or supplies tucked away somewhere concealed.

clue.text: Shout about jellied eel in the salad, perhaps

indicators.note: jellied food is set and reshaped, so the word after it is rearranged
one word placed about another goes around it

blocks.note: to cry is to shout
the letters of this word rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone complains loudly about finding jellied eel in their salad.
explanation.walkthrough: Jellied eels are a traditional London East End dish. The definition is an example: the answer is one thing that might be in a salad.
explanation.definitionFit: This crunchy green stalk vegetable is a common raw ingredient of salads, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Natural cover in garden, originally

blocks.note: surface reading: a plant used as ground cover in a garden from the start
setter's reading: the first garden, Eden, where Adam and Eve covered themselves

explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' could be a first-letters signal, but here it points to the original garden, Eden, where Adam and Eve hid their nakedness.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Adam and Eve sewed together foliage from a tree to cover themselves after the Fall.

clue.text: Upwards of 101 meeting points

indicators.note: in a down clue, going upwards reads the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: the word read backwards
101 in Roman numerals is C (100) plus I (1)

explanation.surface: More than a hundred places where people gather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwards of' looks like 'more than', but 'Upwards' acts on the word 'of' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A focus is a central point where lines or rays converge, and this is the Latin plural.

clue.text: Effective narration

blocks.note: first meaning: striking and significant, as a decisive argument is
second meaning: the act of recounting a story

explanation.surface: A storyteller's powerful account.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark that makes its point strongly is revealing and forceful, and recounting a tale is also its noun form.

clue.text: It does twice daily turns at coastal resorts

definitions.text: It does twice daily turns at coastal resorts

blocks.clueFragment: It does twice daily turns at coastal resorts
blocks.note: surface reading: an entertainer performing two shows a day at seaside theatres
setter's reading: the sea's rise and fall, which reverses direction twice a day

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' suggests variety acts on a seaside pier, but the sea itself turns twice a day.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea rises and falls roughly twice every day under the moon's pull, ebbing and flowing at the shore.

clue.text: Charming hostess, who helped her guests make pigs of themselves

definitions.text: Charming hostess, who helped her guests make pigs of themselves

blocks.clueFragment: Charming hostess, who helped her guests make pigs of themselves
blocks.note: surface reading: a gracious hostess whose guests overeat greedily
setter's reading: casting charms, as the enchantress of the Odyssey literally turned visitors into swine

explanation.walkthrough: In Homer's Odyssey the sorceress on her island turns Odysseus's men into swine; 'charming' means using spells.
explanation.definitionFit: The witch of Greek myth fed Odysseus's crew a drugged meal and transformed them into hogs with her wand.

clue.text: Clothing that is never worn out

definitions.text: Clothing that is never worn out

blocks.clueFragment: Clothing that is never worn out
blocks.note: surface reading: very durable garments that never get threadbare
setter's reading: garments never worn on the outside, being kept beneath other clothes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Worn out' suggests threadbare, but it means worn on the outside or in public view.
explanation.definitionFit: Underclothes such as pants and vests go beneath other garments, so they are not seen in public.
